equipment.name: Lathe Machine
equipment.definition: A lathe is a machine tool that rotates a workpiece about an axis of rotation to perform various operations such as cutting, sanding, drilling, or deformation.
equipment.working_principle: The workpiece is held in a chuck and rotated while a cutting tool is fed into the work causing the cutting action. The tool can move parallel or perpendicular to the axis of rotation.
equipment.exam_notes: Remember: Lathe is the mother of all machine tools. Types: Engine lathe, Turret lathe, Special purpose lathe. Cutting speed formula: V = πDN/1000 m/min

equipment.name: Milling Machine
equipment.definition: A milling machine is a machine tool used for shaping solid materials by removing material from a workpiece using a rotating multi-point cutter.
equipment.working_principle: The cutter rotates at high speed and the workpiece is fed against it. Material is removed in the form of small chips. Can perform face milling and peripheral milling.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Horizontal, Vertical, Universal. Remember indexing methods: Simple, Compound, Differential. Up milling vs Down milling: chip thickness, surface finish, tool life differences.

equipment.name: Drilling Machine
equipment.definition: A drilling machine is used to make cylindrical holes in workpieces using a rotating cutting tool called drill bit.
equipment.working_principle: A rotating drill bit is pressed against the workpiece with sufficient force to cut material and create a hole. Coolant is often used to reduce heat.
applications: Making holes in metal and wood
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Portable, Sensitive, Upright, Radial, Gang, Multiple spindle. Drill nomenclature: Point angle 118°, Helix angle 20-35°. Drill materials: HSS, Carbide.

equipment.name: Grinding Machine
equipment.definition: A grinding machine uses an abrasive wheel as cutting tool to remove small amounts of material from workpiece for finishing operations.
equipment.working_principle: An abrasive grinding wheel rotates at high speed. The workpiece is brought into contact with the wheel which removes material through abrasion.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Surface, Cylindrical, Centerless, Tool and cutter. Wheel designation: Abrasive-Grain size-Grade-Structure-Bond. Dressing and truing operations.

equipment.name: Shaper Machine
equipment.definition: A shaper is a machine tool that uses a single-point cutting tool attached to a reciprocating ram to machine flat surfaces, grooves, and slots.
equipment.working_principle: The ram holding the cutting tool reciprocates over the workpiece. Cutting occurs during forward stroke, return stroke is idle. Workpiece is fed perpendicular to cutting direction.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Horizontal, Vertical, Travelling head. Quick return mechanism: Whitworth, Crank and slotted lever. Cutting stroke slower than return stroke.

equipment.name: CNC Machine
equipment.definition: Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machines are automated machine tools controlled by precisely programmed commands encoded on a storage medium.
equipment.working_principle: A computer controls the motion of cutting tools and workpiece based on programmed instructions (G-codes and M-codes), enabling high precision and repeatability.
equipment.exam_notes: Programming: G-codes (geometric), M-codes (machine). Types: CNC Lathe, Mill, Router. Advantages: Precision, repeatability, complex shapes. APT language.

equipment.name: Welding Machine
equipment.definition: Welding machines provide the necessary heat and electrical current to join metal parts by melting and fusing them together.
equipment.working_principle: Electric arc or gas flame generates intense heat that melts the base metal and filler material, which solidify to form a strong joint.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Arc (MIG, TIG, Stick), Gas (Oxy-acetylene), Resistance (Spot, Seam). Welding positions: Flat, Horizontal, Vertical, Overhead. Defects: Porosity, Undercut, Slag inclusion.

equipment.name: Power Hacksaw
equipment.definition: A power hacksaw is a metal cutting machine that uses a reciprocating blade to cut metal workpieces to desired lengths.
equipment.working_principle: A toothed blade reciprocates rapidly while the workpiece is fed slowly into it. Cutting occurs on the forward stroke with automatic return.
equipment.exam_notes: Blade specifications: TPI (teeth per inch), material (HSS, Bimetal). Cutting speed depends on material hardness. Feed rate control important.

equipment.name: Planer Machine
equipment.definition: A planer is a large machine tool used to produce horizontal, vertical, or inclined flat surfaces by moving the workpiece against a stationary cutting tool.
equipment.working_principle: The workpiece is mounted on a reciprocating table that moves back and forth under stationary cutting tools. Multiple tools can work simultaneously.
equipment.exam_notes: Difference from Shaper: In planer, workpiece moves (tool stationary); in shaper, tool moves (workpiece stationary). Planer for larger workpieces.

equipment.name: Boring Machine
equipment.definition: A boring machine enlarges and finishes existing holes to precise dimensions and accurate alignment using a single-point cutting tool.
equipment.working_principle: A rotating boring bar with cutting tool is fed into a pre-existing hole to enlarge and finish it to required size and surface finish.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Horizontal, Vertical, Jig boring. More accurate than drilling. Used when precision holes >25mm diameter needed. Boring bar rigidity critical.

equipment.name: Hydraulic Press
equipment.definition: A hydraulic press uses hydraulic pressure to compress, bend, or shape materials using Pascal's principle of fluid pressure transmission.
equipment.working_principle: Hydraulic fluid under pressure acts on a piston creating large compressive force. Force multiplication achieved through different piston areas (F2/F1 = A2/A1).
equipment.exam_notes: Pascal's Law: P=F/A. Mechanical advantage = A2/A1. Types: H-frame, C-frame, 4-column. Tonnage capacity varies. Safety: pressure relief valves essential.

equipment.name: EDM Machine
equipment.definition: Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM) removes material through electrical sparks between the electrode and workpiece in a dielectric fluid.
equipment.working_principle: Rapid recurring electrical discharges create sparks that melt and vaporize tiny particles from the workpiece surface. No mechanical contact required.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Die-sinking EDM, Wire EDM. Materials: Must be electrically conductive. Dielectric fluid: Kerosene, deionized water. No tool wear for hard materials.

equipment.name: Broaching Machine
equipment.definition: A broaching machine uses a multi-toothed cutting tool (broach) to remove material in a single linear pass to create precise internal or external surfaces.
equipment.working_principle: A broach with successively larger teeth is pulled or pushed through/over the workpiece, each tooth removing a small layer of material.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Internal, External, Surface. Advantages: High accuracy, good surface finish, high production rate. Each broach limited to one size/shape.

equipment.name: Slotting Machine
equipment.definition: A slotting machine is a vertical shaper used to cut slots, keyways, and internal surfaces using a reciprocating single-point cutting tool.
equipment.working_principle: The ram moves vertically in a reciprocating motion. The cutting tool moves downward for cutting stroke and returns upward as idle stroke.
equipment.exam_notes: Also called vertical shaper. Quick return mechanism similar to shaper. Rotary table allows circular work. Used where planer/shaper cannot reach.

equipment.name: Hobbing Machine
equipment.definition: A gear hobbing machine cuts gears and splines by rotating the workpiece and the hob (cutting tool) in synchronized motion.
equipment.working_principle: The hob (cylindrical gear-shaped cutter) and blank rotate continuously with precise speed ratio. The hob is gradually fed across the blank face to generate gear teeth.
equipment.exam_notes: Hobbing is a continuous indexing process. Speed ratio = Teeth on gear/Starts on hob. Can produce multiple teeth simultaneously. Most economical for quantity production.

equipment.name: 3D Printer (Additive Manufacturing)
equipment.definition: A 3D printer creates three-dimensional objects by depositing material layer-by-layer based on digital CAD models.
equipment.working_principle: Material (plastic, metal, resin) is deposited, sintered, or solidified layer by layer following computer-controlled paths to build the final 3D object.
equipment.exam_notes: Technologies: FDM (Fused Deposition), SLA (Stereolithography), SLS (Selective Laser Sintering), DMLS (Direct Metal Laser Sintering). Materials: PLA, ABS, Nylon, Metals.

equipment.name: Sand Blasting Machine
equipment.definition: A sand blasting machine propels abrasive materials against a surface under high pressure to clean, etch, or finish the surface.
equipment.working_principle: Compressed air accelerates abrasive media through a nozzle onto the workpiece surface, removing contaminants, rust, or creating surface texture.
equipment.exam_notes: Abrasives: Sand, glass beads, steel grit, aluminum oxide. Pressure: 60-125 PSI. Safety: Dust hazard, wear protective gear. Wet blasting reduces dust.

equipment.name: Forging Hammer
equipment.definition: A forging hammer shapes metal by repeated impact blows, compressing and forming the material while hot.
equipment.working_principle: A heavy hammer (ram) is repeatedly raised and dropped onto the heated workpiece placed on an anvil, deforming it into desired shape.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Power hammer (steam, hydraulic, pneumatic), Drop hammer. Forging temperature: Steel 1200°C. Grain structure improved. Compare with press forging.

equipment.name: Rolling Mill
equipment.definition: A rolling mill shapes metal by passing it between rotating rolls that compress and elongate the material.
equipment.working_principle: Metal is fed between two or more rotating rolls. The gap between rolls determines final thickness. Material is elongated and reduced in cross-section.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Two-high, Three-high, Four-high, Cluster mill. Hot rolling (>recrystallization temp), Cold rolling (<recrystallization). Reduction ratio, draft calculation.

equipment.name: Heat Treatment Furnace
equipment.definition: Heat treatment furnaces heat metals to specific temperatures and cool them in controlled manner to alter their microstructure and properties.
equipment.working_principle: Controlled heating to specific temperature, holding (soaking), and cooling at predetermined rates to achieve desired mechanical properties like hardness, strength, ductility.
equipment.exam_notes: Processes: Annealing (soft), Normalizing (refine grain), Hardening (increase hardness), Tempering (reduce brittleness). TTT diagrams, CCT curves. Martensite, Pearlite, Bainite structures.

equipment.name: Ultrasonic Machining
equipment.definition: Ultrasonic machining removes material using abrasive particles driven by ultrasonic vibrations of a tool against the workpiece.
equipment.working_principle: A tool vibrates at ultrasonic frequency (20kHz) with small amplitude. Abrasive slurry between tool and workpiece causes material removal through impact.
equipment.exam_notes: Non-traditional machining. Works on hard brittle materials. No thermal or chemical damage. MRR low. Abrasives: Boron carbide, silicon carbide, aluminum oxide.

equipment.name: Transformer
equipment.definition: A transformer is a static electrical device that transfers electrical energy between two or more circuits through electromagnetic induction.
equipment.working_principle: Based on Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction. When AC flows through primary winding, it creates changing magnetic flux in the core which induces voltage in secondary winding.
equipment.exam_notes: Transformation ratio: V2/V1 = N2/N1 = I1/I2. Losses: Core losses (Hysteresis + Eddy current) and Copper losses (I²R). Efficiency typically 95-99%. Tests: OC test, SC test.

equipment.name: DC Motor
equipment.definition: A DC motor is an electrical machine that converts direct current electrical energy into mechanical energy through the interaction of magnetic fields.
equipment.working_principle: When current-carrying conductor is placed in a magnetic field, it experiences a force (Fleming's Left Hand Rule). The commutator ensures continuous rotation by reversing current direction.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Series, Shunt, Compound motors. Back EMF: Eb = V - IaRa. Torque: T ∝ ΦIa. Speed control: Flux control, Armature voltage control, Resistance control. Starting: 3-point, 4-point starter.

equipment.name: Alternator (AC Generator)
equipment.definition: An alternator is a synchronous generator that converts mechanical energy into alternating current electrical energy using electromagnetic induction.
equipment.working_principle: A rotating magnetic field (rotor) cuts stationary armature windings (stator), inducing AC voltage. Frequency determined by speed and number of poles: f = PN/120.
equipment.exam_notes: EMF equation: E = 4.44fΦNKpKd. Types: Salient pole, Non-salient pole. Synchronous speed: Ns = 120f/P. Voltage regulation, Parallel operation, Hunting phenomenon.

equipment.name: Induction Motor
equipment.definition: An induction motor is an AC motor where electric current in the rotor is induced by electromagnetic induction from the magnetic field of the stator winding.
equipment.working_principle: Rotating magnetic field in stator induces current in rotor conductors. This current creates rotor magnetic field that interacts with stator field producing torque.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Squirrel cage, Slip ring. Slip: s = (Ns - N)/Ns. Torque-slip characteristics. Starting methods: DOL, Star-delta, Auto-transformer, Rotor resistance. Speed control: V/f, pole changing.

equipment.name: Circuit Breaker
equipment.definition: A circuit breaker is an automatically operated electrical switch designed to protect an electrical circuit from damage caused by overload or short circuit.
equipment.working_principle: Detects fault conditions and interrupts current flow by separating contacts. Arc is quenched using various mediums (oil, air, SF6, vacuum).
equipment.exam_notes: Types by voltage: LV, MV, HV, EHV. By medium: Oil (Bulk, Minimum), Air blast, SF6, Vacuum. Arc quenching methods. Breaking capacity, Making capacity. Time-current characteristics.

equipment.name: Relay
equipment.definition: An electrical relay is an electromagnetic switch operated by a relatively small electric current that can turn on or off a much larger electric current.
equipment.working_principle: When current flows through the coil, it creates a magnetic field that attracts the armature, closing or opening contacts to control another circuit.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Electromagnetic, Thermal, Static (digital). Protection relays: Overcurrent, Differential, Distance, Directional. Pickup value, Reset value, Operating time. CT, PT for sensing.

equipment.name: Battery Charger
equipment.definition: A battery charger is a device used to put energy into a secondary cell or rechargeable battery by forcing an electric current through it.
equipment.working_principle: Converts AC to DC using rectifiers, regulates voltage and current to charge battery according to its chemistry and state of charge.
equipment.exam_notes: Charging methods: Constant current, Constant voltage, Taper charging, Pulse charging. C-rate (1C = battery capacity in 1 hour). Overcharging protection. Li-ion, Lead-acid characteristics.

equipment.name: Inverter
equipment.definition: An inverter is a power electronic device that converts direct current (DC) to alternating current (AC).
equipment.working_principle: Uses electronic switches (IGBTs, MOSFETs) operated by control circuits to convert DC to AC. PWM techniques create sinusoidal output from DC input.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Voltage source, Current source. By phase: Single-phase, Three-phase. Topology: Half-bridge, Full-bridge, Three-level. PWM: SPWM, SVPWM. THD, switching frequency.

equipment.name: Power Factor Correction Unit
equipment.definition: A power factor correction unit improves the power factor of an electrical system by reducing reactive power demand using capacitor banks or active compensation.
equipment.working_principle: Capacitors supply reactive power locally, reducing the reactive power drawn from the supply. Automatic switching based on load conditions.
equipment.exam_notes: Power Factor = cosφ = kW/kVA. Low PF causes: Inductive loads, underloaded motors. Benefits: Reduced losses, increased capacity. kVAR required = kW(tanφ1 - tanφ2). Automatic PFC panels.

equipment.name: Servo Motor
equipment.definition: A servo motor is a rotary or linear actuator that allows for precise control of angular or linear position, velocity, and acceleration.
equipment.working_principle: Receives control signal indicating desired position, compares with actual position from encoder feedback, and adjusts to minimize error through closed-loop control.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: DC servo, AC servo, Brushless servo. Position control via PWM signal. Encoder: Incremental, Absolute. PID control algorithm. Holding torque, dynamic torque.

equipment.name: Megger (Insulation Tester)
equipment.definition: A megger is an instrument used to measure the electrical resistance of insulators to ensure the insulation integrity of electrical systems and equipment.
equipment.working_principle: Applies a high DC voltage (500V-5000V) to the insulation and measures the resulting leakage current. Resistance calculated using Ohm's law (R = V/I).
equipment.exam_notes: Test voltages: 250V, 500V, 1000V, 2500V, 5000V. Insulation resistance in MΩ. Polarization index (PI) = R10min/R1min. Temperature affects readings. DAR test.

equipment.name: SMPS (Switched Mode Power Supply)
equipment.definition: An SMPS is an electronic power supply that incorporates a switching regulator to convert electrical power efficiently using high-frequency switching.
equipment.working_principle: Input AC is rectified to DC, then chopped at high frequency (20-100kHz), transformed, rectified again, and filtered to produce stable DC output.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Buck, Boost, Buck-boost, Flyback, Forward converter. Advantages: High efficiency (80-95%), compact size. PWM control. Switching losses, EMI issues.

equipment.name: Synchronous Motor
equipment.definition: A synchronous motor is an AC motor where the rotor rotates at synchronous speed (same as the rotating magnetic field) regardless of load.
equipment.working_principle: DC excitation creates fixed magnetic poles on rotor. These lock with the rotating magnetic field of stator and rotate at exactly synchronous speed.
equipment.exam_notes: Speed: N = 120f/P (constant). V-curves, Inverted V-curves. Starting: Damper winding, VFD. Power factor control by excitation. Hunting, synchronizing power.

equipment.name: Stepper Motor
equipment.definition: A stepper motor is a brushless DC motor that divides a full rotation into a number of equal steps, moving in discrete steps based on digital pulses.
equipment.working_principle: Coils are energized in sequence creating a rotating magnetic field. Rotor aligns with each field position, moving in precise angular increments.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Permanent magnet, Variable reluctance, Hybrid. Step angle = 360°/(rotor teeth × phases). Unipolar, Bipolar. Driving modes: Full step, Half step, Microstepping. Holding torque.

equipment.name: Voltage Stabilizer
equipment.definition: A voltage stabilizer is a device that provides constant output voltage despite variations in input voltage or load conditions.
equipment.working_principle: Uses servo motor-driven variable transformer (auto-transformer) or electronic switching to tap different transformer windings, maintaining constant output voltage.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Servo-controlled, Static (Relay-based), Electronic/Digital. Correction time, response time. Input voltage range typically ±30-40%. Output regulation ±1-5%.

equipment.name: Current Transformer (CT)
equipment.definition: A current transformer is an instrument transformer that produces an alternating current in its secondary proportional to the AC being measured in its primary.
equipment.working_principle: Primary (few turns or single conductor) carries load current. This induces proportional current in secondary (many turns) based on turns ratio. Secondary never open-circuited.
equipment.exam_notes: Ratio: Ip/Is = Ns/Np. Accuracy class: 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 3, 5. Never open secondary (high voltage). Burden: Connected impedance. Knee point voltage. Bar-type, Wound-type, Core-balance CT.

equipment.name: Potential Transformer (PT/VT)
equipment.definition: A potential transformer is an instrument transformer used to transform high voltage to a lower, measurable voltage proportional to the voltage being measured.
equipment.working_principle: Step-down transformer with precise ratio. Primary connected across high voltage, secondary provides safe, proportional low voltage for instruments.
equipment.exam_notes: Ratio: Vp/Vs = Np/Ns. Standard secondary: 110V (phase), 110/√3 V (line). Accuracy class: 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 3. Burden: VA rating. Capacitor VT for EHV systems.

equipment.name: Lightning Arrester
equipment.definition: A lightning arrester is a protective device that diverts high-voltage surges caused by lightning or switching operations to ground, protecting equipment.
equipment.working_principle: Contains voltage-dependent resistors (metal oxide varistors). During surge, resistance drops dramatically, providing low-impedance path to ground. Returns to high resistance after surge.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Rod gap, Horn gap, Multi-gap, Valve-type, Metal oxide (MOV). Parameters: Rated voltage, MCOV (Max continuous operating voltage), Discharge current, Energy absorption capability.

equipment.name: Energy Meter
equipment.definition: An energy meter is an instrument used to measure the amount of electrical energy consumed by a residence, business, or electrically powered device.
equipment.working_principle: Measures both voltage and current continuously. Multiplies instantaneous values and integrates over time to calculate energy (kWh). Digital meters use microprocessors.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Electromechanical (induction), Electronic, Smart meters. Units: kWh. Meter constant: Rev/kWh. Errors: Friction, phase, creeping. Testing: Phantom loading, direct loading.

equipment.name: Capacitor Bank
equipment.definition: A capacitor bank is a group of several capacitors connected in series or parallel used to store electrical energy and improve power factor.
equipment.working_principle: Capacitors store energy in electric field and supply reactive power (kVAR) to compensate for lagging power factor caused by inductive loads.
equipment.exam_notes: Reactive power: Q = V²/Xc = V²ωC. Connection: Star, Delta. Automatic power factor correction. Detuned reactor to avoid resonance. kVAR calculation for target PF.

equipment.name: UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply)
equipment.definition: A UPS is an electrical apparatus that provides emergency power to a load when the input power source fails, typically using batteries.
equipment.working_principle: During normal operation, battery is charged and load is powered. On power failure, inverter converts battery DC to AC instantly. Seamless switchover in online UPS.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Offline (Standby), Line-interactive, Online (Double conversion). Backup time calculation. VA rating vs W rating. Power factor. Lead-acid vs Li-ion batteries.

equipment.name: Theodolite
equipment.definition: A theodolite is a precision optical instrument used for measuring horizontal and vertical angles in surveying and engineering applications.
equipment.working_principle: Uses a rotating telescope mounted on horizontal and vertical axes. Angles are measured using graduated circles and vernier scales or digital displays with high precision.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Transit theodolite, Non-transit theodolite, Digital theodolite. Temporary adjustments: Leveling, Centering, Focusing. Permanent adjustments. Least count = Value of 1 div / No. of divisions on vernier. Errors and precautions.

equipment.name: Total Station
equipment.definition: A total station is an electronic/optical surveying instrument that integrates electronic theodolite with electronic distance meter (EDM) and processes data internally.
equipment.working_principle: Combines angle measurement (electronic theodolite) with distance measurement (EDM using electromagnetic waves). Microprocessor calculates coordinates, elevations, and can store data digitally.
equipment.exam_notes: Advantages: Faster, more accurate, direct data storage, calculates coordinates automatically. Accuracy: Angle ±2-5 seconds, Distance ±2mm±2ppm. Robotic total station. Data download to CAD.

equipment.name: Dumpy Level
equipment.definition: A dumpy level is a surveying instrument used for establishing or checking points in the same horizontal plane and measuring height differences.
equipment.working_principle: Telescope with cross-hairs provides line of sight. After leveling, this line of sight is horizontal. Staff readings at different points give relative elevations.
equipment.exam_notes: Temporary adjustments: Setting up, Leveling, Focusing, Elimination of parallax. Permanent adjustments: Two peg test. Types of leveling: Differential, Profile, Reciprocal. Height of collimation method, Rise and fall method.

equipment.name: Auto Level
equipment.definition: An automatic level (auto level) is a surveying leveling instrument that automatically levels the line of sight using a compensator mechanism.
equipment.working_principle: After rough leveling using circular bubble, internal compensator (gravity-controlled pendulum system) automatically makes line of sight horizontal.
equipment.exam_notes: Advantages over dumpy level: Faster, self-leveling, less operator error. Accuracy: ±0.5mm to ±3mm per km double run. Check compensator working regularly. Magnification typically 20x-32x.

equipment.name: GPS/GNSS Receiver
equipment.definition: A GNSS receiver is a satellite-based positioning device that determines precise location coordinates using signals from multiple satellite systems.
equipment.working_principle: Receives signals from 4 or more satellites. Calculates position using trilateration based on signal travel time. Corrections from base station improve accuracy (RTK/PPK).
equipment.exam_notes: Systems: GPS (USA), GLONASS (Russia), Galileo (EU), BeiDou (China). Accuracy: Static (mm), RTK (cm), Autonomous (m). DOP factors. Base-rover setup. Post-processing.

equipment.name: Concrete Mixer
equipment.definition: A concrete mixer is a machine that homogeneously combines cement, aggregate (sand, gravel), and water to form concrete for construction.
equipment.working_principle: Rotating drum with blades mixes ingredients. Tilting drum type discharges by tilting, non-tilting type by reversing rotation or using chute.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Batch mixers (Tilting, Non-tilting, Reverse drum, Forced), Continuous mixers. Capacity: 0.25m³ to 3m³ typical. Mix design, W/C ratio, Slump test, Mixing time.

equipment.name: Vibrator (Concrete)
equipment.definition: A concrete vibrator is used to consolidate fresh concrete by removing trapped air voids and ensuring uniform compaction for increased strength and durability.
equipment.working_principle: High-frequency vibrations (typically 10,000-15,000 vibrations/min) reduce internal friction between concrete particles, allowing them to settle densely and expel air.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Internal (needle/poker), External (formwork), Surface (screed). Frequency: 10,000-18,000 VPM. Radius of action: 30-50cm. Over-vibration causes segregation. Insert vertically, slow withdrawal.

equipment.name: Compactor (Soil/Road Roller)
equipment.definition: A compactor is a construction machine used to compress soil, gravel, concrete, or asphalt to increase density and load-bearing capacity.
equipment.working_principle: Applies static weight and/or vibration to compress material layers. Repeated passes progressively densify material by expelling air voids.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Smooth wheel, Pneumatic tyred, Sheepsfoot, Vibratory, Tandem. Suitable for different soils. Field density tests: Sand replacement, Core cutter. Compaction curve, OMC, MDD.

equipment.name: Compression Testing Machine (CTM)
equipment.definition: A compression testing machine (CTM) is used to determine the compressive strength of concrete cubes, cylinders, and other construction materials.
equipment.working_principle: Applies gradually increasing compressive load on specimen between two platens until failure. Load at failure divided by cross-sectional area gives compressive strength.
equipment.exam_notes: Cube size: 150mm × 150mm × 150mm standard. Curing: 7 days, 28 days. Loading rate: 140 kg/cm²/min. Compressive strength formula: σc = P/A. M20, M25, M30 grade concrete.

equipment.name: Universal Testing Machine (UTM)
equipment.definition: A universal testing machine (UTM) performs tensile, compression, bending, and shear tests on various materials to determine mechanical properties.
equipment.working_principle: Applies controlled force/displacement on specimen. Load cells and extensometers measure force and deformation. Stress-strain curves generated.
equipment.exam_notes: Tests: Tensile (yield strength, ultimate strength, % elongation), Compression, Bending (flexural strength). Stress-strain curve. Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio. IS codes for testing.

equipment.name: Slump Cone Test Apparatus
equipment.definition: Slump cone test apparatus measures the workability and consistency of fresh concrete before it sets.
equipment.working_principle: Fresh concrete filled in standard cone mold, tamped in layers, cone lifted vertically. The slump (vertical settlement) indicates workability.
equipment.exam_notes: Cone dimensions: Top 100mm, Bottom 200mm, Height 300mm. Slump types: True slump, Shear slump, Collapse slump. Slump values: 0-25mm (very low), 50-100mm (medium), 100-150mm (high). Affects: W/C ratio, aggregate grading.

equipment.name: Oven (Materials Testing)
equipment.definition: A laboratory oven is used to dry soil, aggregate, and other construction materials to constant mass for determining moisture content and other properties.
equipment.working_principle: Maintains controlled temperature (typically 105-110°C) to evaporate moisture from samples without decomposing or altering material properties.
equipment.exam_notes: Standard temperature: 105-110°C for soil. Drying to constant mass (weight change <0.1% in 4 hours). Water content = (Wet weight - Dry weight)/Dry weight × 100%. IS codes: IS 2720.

equipment.name: Sieve Shaker
equipment.definition: A sieve shaker is a mechanical device used to separate particles of different sizes in soil and aggregate samples for gradation analysis.
equipment.working_principle: Stack of sieves with decreasing mesh size vibrates mechanically. Particles pass through sieves according to size, separating into fractions.
equipment.exam_notes: IS sieve sizes: 80mm, 40mm, 20mm, 10mm, 4.75mm, 2.36mm, 1.18mm, 600µ, 300µ, 150µ, 75µ. Sieve analysis: Cumulative % retained, % passing. Grading curves. Fineness modulus.

equipment.name: Proctor Compaction Test Apparatus
equipment.definition: Proctor compaction test apparatus determines the optimum moisture content (OMC) and maximum dry density (MDD) of soil for compaction specifications.
equipment.working_principle: Soil samples at various moisture contents are compacted in a mold using standard energy. Dry density plotted against moisture content gives compaction curve.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Standard Proctor (light), Modified Proctor (heavy). Rammer drop: 310mm (standard), 450mm (modified). Layers: 3 (standard), 5 (modified). Blows/layer: 25. Compaction curve peak gives OMC & MDD.

equipment.name: Direct Shear Test Apparatus
equipment.definition: Direct shear test apparatus determines the shear strength parameters (cohesion and angle of internal friction) of soil samples.
equipment.working_principle: Soil specimen placed in split box. Normal load applied vertically. Horizontal shear force gradually increased until failure occurs along horizontal plane.
equipment.exam_notes: Shear strength: τ = c + σtanφ (Mohr-Coulomb). Tests at different normal stresses. Plot τ vs σ, slope = tanφ, intercept = c. Drained vs undrained conditions. IS 2720 Part 13.

equipment.name: CBR Test Apparatus
equipment.definition: California Bearing Ratio (CBR) test apparatus measures the bearing capacity of soil and aggregates for pavement design.
equipment.working_principle: Penetration plunger pushed into compacted soil specimen at controlled rate. Load required for penetration compared to standard crushed stone (100% CBR).
equipment.exam_notes: CBR = (Test load/Standard load) × 100%. Penetrations: 2.5mm, 5mm. Standard load: 1370kg (2.5mm), 2055kg (5mm). CBR values: <3% (very poor), 3-7% (poor to fair), 7-20% (fair), >20% (good). Soaked vs unsoaked.

equipment.name: Triaxial Test Apparatus
equipment.definition: Triaxial test apparatus determines shear strength, stress-strain behavior, and other mechanical properties of soil under controlled stress conditions.
equipment.working_principle: Cylindrical soil specimen enclosed in rubber membrane, subjected to confining pressure (cell pressure) and axial loading. Drainage and pore pressure can be controlled.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: UU (Unconsolidated Undrained), CU (Consolidated Undrained), CD (Consolidated Drained). Mohr circle analysis. Effective stress, Pore pressure. φ and c determination more accurate than direct shear.

equipment.name: Plate Load Test Apparatus
equipment.definition: Plate load test apparatus determines the bearing capacity and settlement characteristics of soil in-situ at foundation level.
equipment.working_principle: Rigid steel plate loaded incrementally on prepared soil surface. Settlement measured at each load increment. Load-settlement curve analyzed for bearing capacity.
equipment.exam_notes: Ultimate bearing capacity at settlement = plate diameter/10. Safe bearing capacity = UBC/FOS. Plate sizes for different foundations. Load increments, holding time. Settlement rate <0.02mm/min for next loading.

equipment.name: Plumb Bob
equipment.definition: A plumb bob is a simple tool consisting of a weight suspended from a string, used to establish a true vertical reference line.
equipment.working_principle: Gravity pulls the weight directly downward, creating a perfectly vertical line. The string shows true vertical regardless of surrounding structures.
equipment.exam_notes: Essential for setting instruments over survey points. Wind affects accuracy. Laser plumb bobs now available for high-rise. Used with theodolite for precise centering over stations.

equipment.name: Paver Machine (Asphalt)
equipment.definition: An asphalt paver is a construction machine used to lay asphalt concrete on roads, parking lots, and other surfaces uniformly and efficiently.
equipment.working_principle: Receives hot asphalt from dump trucks into hopper, conveys it to rear, spreads uniformly via screed which also provides initial compaction and smooth finish.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Tracked, Wheeled. Screed: Fixed width, Extendable. Paving width: 2.5m to 12m. Thickness: 25mm to 300mm. Temperature control critical. Grade and slope control systems. Compaction follows immediately.

equipment.name: Excavator
equipment.definition: An excavator is a heavy construction machine consisting of a boom, dipper, bucket and cab on a rotating platform, used for excavation and material handling.
equipment.working_principle: Hydraulic cylinders control boom, arm, and bucket movements. Rotating superstructure allows 360° operation. Operator controls from cab using joysticks.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Crawler, Wheeled, Mini excavator. Bucket capacity: 0.2 m³ to 5 m³. Attachments: Breaker, Grapple, Auger. Operating radius, digging depth, reach specifications. Hourly output calculation.

equipment.name: Oscilloscope
equipment.definition: An oscilloscope is an electronic test instrument that graphically displays varying electrical voltages as a two-dimensional plot of voltage versus time.
equipment.working_principle: Input signal applied to vertical deflection system. Time base generator creates horizontal sweep. CRT/LCD displays waveform. Digital scopes sample and store signal digitally.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Analog (CRT-based), Digital Storage Oscilloscope (DSO), Mixed Signal Oscilloscope (MSO). Key specs: Bandwidth, Sample rate, Rise time. Trigger modes: Auto, Normal, Single. Measurements: Vpp, Vrms, frequency, duty cycle.

equipment.name: Function Generator
equipment.definition: A function generator is an electronic instrument that produces various types of electrical waveforms over a wide range of frequencies for testing circuits.
equipment.working_principle: Uses oscillator circuits (RC, LC, or crystal controlled) to generate periodic waveforms. Waveform shaping circuits convert basic oscillations to desired shapes (sine, square, triangle).
equipment.exam_notes: Common waveforms: Sine, Square, Triangle, Sawtooth, Pulse, Ramp. Frequency range: mHz to MHz. Parameters: Frequency, Amplitude, DC offset, Duty cycle, Symmetry. Arbitrary waveform generators (AWG) for complex signals.

equipment.name: Power Supply (DC Bench)
equipment.definition: A bench power supply is a laboratory instrument that provides stable, adjustable DC voltage and current for powering and testing electronic circuits.
equipment.working_principle: AC mains converted to DC via transformer, rectifier, filter. Linear or switching regulation maintains constant voltage/current. Feedback loop corrects for load variations.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Linear (low noise, low efficiency), Switching (high efficiency, compact). Modes: Constant Voltage (CV), Constant Current (CC). Specs: Voltage range, Current capacity, Ripple, Load/Line regulation. Multi-channel supplies.

equipment.name: Multimeter (Digital)
equipment.definition: A digital multimeter (DMM) is a portable electronic measuring instrument that combines several measurement functions including voltage, current, and resistance.
equipment.working_principle: Converts analog input signal to digital using ADC. Microcontroller processes and displays result on LCD/LED. Range selection and function switches configure internal circuits.
equipment.exam_notes: True RMS vs Average sensing. Auto-ranging vs Manual. Accuracy: ± (% of reading + digits). Input impedance: 10MΩ for voltage. Safety rating: CAT I, II, III, IV. Hold, Min/Max, Rel functions.

equipment.name: Breadboard
equipment.definition: A breadboard is a reusable solderless device used to build temporary prototypes and test electronic circuits without soldering components.
equipment.working_principle: Contains spring clips underneath holes arranged in rows and columns. Components inserted into holes make electrical connections through clips. Power rails run along sides.
equipment.exam_notes: Typical size: 830 tie points. Terminal strips (5 holes connected), Power strips (entire row connected). Limited to low frequency (<10MHz) due to parasitic capacitance. Max current ~1-2A. Jumper wires (solid core, 22-26 AWG).

equipment.name: Soldering Station
equipment.definition: A soldering station is a temperature-controlled tool used to join electronic components to PCBs by melting solder to create electrical and mechanical connections.
equipment.working_principle: Heating element in iron tip controlled by temperature feedback loop. Thermocouple or sensor monitors tip temperature. Controller maintains set temperature ±1-5°C.
equipment.exam_notes: Temperature: 300-400°C typical. Lead-free solder needs higher temp (350-380°C) than leaded (320-350°C). Tip types: Chisel, Conical, Bevel. Flux removes oxidation. Solder: 60/40 (Sn/Pb), SAC305 (lead-free). ESD-safe stations.

equipment.name: Logic Analyzer
equipment.definition: A logic analyzer is an electronic instrument that captures and displays multiple digital signals simultaneously, showing timing relationships and protocol decoding.
equipment.working_principle: Samples multiple digital channels at high speed, stores data in memory. Triggers on specific patterns. Displays timing diagram showing state changes of all channels.
equipment.exam_notes: Sample rate: MHz to GHz. Channels: 8 to 100+. Trigger types: Edge, Pattern, Glitch, Setup/Hold. Mixed Signal Oscilloscope (MSO) combines analog + logic channels. Protocol decoders essential for serial buses.

equipment.name: Spectrum Analyzer
equipment.definition: A spectrum analyzer measures and displays the frequency spectrum of signals, showing signal power versus frequency rather than voltage versus time.
equipment.working_principle: Superheterodyne technique: Input signal mixed with local oscillator, filtered, detected. Sweeping LO scans frequency range. Displays amplitude vs frequency.
equipment.exam_notes: Key parameters: Frequency range, Resolution Bandwidth (RBW), Noise floor, Dynamic range. Types: Swept-tuned, FFT-based, Real-time. Markers, Peak search. Applications: Wireless, Radar, Satellite communications.

equipment.name: LCR Meter
equipment.definition: An LCR meter measures inductance (L), capacitance (C), and resistance (R) of electronic components with high accuracy across various frequencies.
equipment.working_principle: Applies AC test signal of known frequency and amplitude to component. Measures resulting voltage and phase. Calculates impedance, then L, C, or R from impedance and phase.
equipment.exam_notes: Test frequencies: 100Hz to 100kHz typical. Parameters measured: L, C, R, Z, D (dissipation), Q (quality factor), ESR (equivalent series resistance). Series/Parallel mode. Kelvin (4-wire) probes for accuracy.

equipment.name: Hot Air Rework Station
equipment.definition: A hot air rework station uses controlled heated air flow to remove and install surface mount components on PCBs without damaging surrounding components.
equipment.working_principle: Heater element warms air, fan blows it through nozzle. Temperature and airflow controlled independently. Focused hot air melts solder for component removal/placement.
equipment.exam_notes: Temperature range: 100-500°C. Air flow: 1-99 L/min adjustable. Nozzle sizes for different component sizes. Lead-free temperatures higher. Preheat PCB to avoid thermal shock. ESD-safe models.

equipment.name: IC Tester
equipment.definition: An IC tester is a device that verifies the functionality of integrated circuits by applying test patterns and comparing outputs with expected results.
equipment.working_principle: Applies input test vectors to IC pins, reads outputs, compares with truth table or expected patterns. Indicates pass/fail for each test condition.
equipment.exam_notes: Types: Logic IC tester (digital), Analog IC tester, Universal IC tester. Tests: Truth table verification, Propagation delay, Fan-out. Common ICs: 74xx series, 40xx CMOS, Timers, Op-amps.

equipment.name: Microcontroller Development Board
equipment.definition: A microcontroller development board is a PCB containing a microcontroller along with support circuitry, programmer/debugger interface, and I/O connections for prototyping embedded systems.
equipment.working_principle: Microcontroller executes programmed instructions. Support circuits provide power regulation, clock, reset. GPIO pins connect to external components. USB/Serial interface for programming.
equipment.exam_notes: Popular platforms: Arduino (ATmega328P, ARM Cortex), ESP32/ESP8266 (WiFi), STM32 (ARM), Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040). IDEs: Arduino IDE, Keil, STM32CubeIDE. Protocols: GPIO, UART, SPI, I2C, PWM, ADC.

equipment.name: FPGA Development Board
equipment.definition: An FPGA development board contains a Field-Programmable Gate Array chip along with peripherals, interfaces, and I/O for designing and testing digital logic circuits.
equipment.working_principle: FPGA configured using HDL (Verilog/VHDL). Logic blocks and interconnects programmed to implement custom digital circuits. Reconfigurable for different designs.
equipment.exam_notes: Popular FPGAs: Xilinx (Artix, Spartan), Intel/Altera (Cyclone, MAX). HDL: Verilog, VHDL, SystemVerilog. Tools: Vivado, Quartus. LUTs, Flip-flops, Block RAM, DSP blocks. Soft processors (MicroBlaze, NIOS).

equipment.name: Digital Storage Oscilloscope (DSO)
equipment.definition: A Digital Storage Oscilloscope (DSO) is an advanced oscilloscope that digitizes analog signals using ADCs, stores them in memory, and displays on digital screen with extensive analysis features.
equipment.working_principle: Input signal sampled by high-speed ADC, converted to digital data, stored in memory. DSP processes data. Microcontroller manages display, measurements, and user interface.
equipment.exam_notes: Advantages over analog: Storage, pre-trigger, math functions, automated measurements. Sampling: Real-time, Equivalent-time. Sample rate vs Bandwidth (5-10x rule). Aliasing. Record length. FFT for frequency domain.

equipment.name: PCB Etching System
equipment.definition: A PCB etching system removes unwanted copper from printed circuit boards using chemical etchants, leaving only the desired circuit traces.
equipment.working_principle: Etchant (Ferric Chloride or Ammonium Persulfate) chemically dissolves exposed copper. Resist (photoresist or marker) protects desired traces. Agitation speeds up process.
equipment.exam_notes: Methods: Chemical etching (FeCl3, CuCl2), Photo-etching (UV exposure + developer). Steps: Design → Print → Transfer → Etch → Drill → Solder. Etch rate depends on temperature, concentration, agitation. Disposal of waste etchant.

equipment.name: UV PCB Exposure Unit
equipment.definition: A UV exposure unit transfers circuit patterns onto photosensitive PCB boards by exposing them to ultraviolet light through a photomask.
equipment.working_principle: UV light passes through transparent areas of photomask/film, exposing photoresist on copper board. Exposed areas harden (negative resist) or soften (positive resist). Developer removes soft resist.
equipment.exam_notes: Exposure time: 1-10 minutes depending on lamp power, resist type, distance. Photoresist types: Positive (exposed area removed), Negative (exposed area remains). Resolution: Fine traces <0.2mm possible. Transparency film vs Acetate for mask.

equipment.name: Signal Generator (RF)
equipment.definition: An RF signal generator produces high-frequency signals with precise frequency, amplitude, and modulation for testing and characterizing RF and microwave circuits.
equipment.working_principle: Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) synthesizer generates stable frequency. Modulation circuits add AM, FM, or phase modulation. Output amplitude precisely controlled.
equipment.exam_notes: Frequency range: kHz to GHz. Modulation types: AM, FM, PM, Pulse. Output level: -140dBm to +20dBm typical. Specs: Frequency accuracy, Phase noise, Harmonics. Vector signal generators for complex modulation.

equipment.name: Network Analyzer (VNA)
equipment.definition: A Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) measures the network parameters (S-parameters) of RF and microwave components, characterizing their amplitude and phase response.
equipment.working_principle: Sweeps frequency, measures incident and reflected signals at ports. Calculates S-parameters (S11, S12, S21, S22) showing gain, loss, match, and isolation.
equipment.exam_notes: Ports: 2-port (most common), 4-port. S-parameters: S11 (input return loss), S21 (forward transmission), S12 (reverse transmission), S22 (output return loss). Smith chart plots impedance. Calibration: SOLT, TRL.

equipment.name: Power Quality Analyzer
equipment.definition: A power quality analyzer monitors and records electrical power parameters to detect and analyze disturbances, harmonics, and power quality issues.
equipment.working_principle: Simultaneously samples voltage and current waveforms at high speed. Calculates RMS, harmonics, power, power factor, flicker, transients, and other parameters. Records events.
equipment.exam_notes: Measurements: THD, Individual harmonics, Voltage flicker, Sag, Swell, Interruption, Unbalance. Standards: IEC 61000, IEEE 519. Class A, Class S instruments. Phasor diagrams, Trend analysis, Event capture.

equipment.name: Thermal Imaging Camera
equipment.definition: A thermal imaging camera detects infrared radiation (heat) and creates visual images showing temperature distribution, useful for identifying hot spots in electronic circuits.
equipment.working_principle: Infrared detector array senses thermal radiation from objects. Electronics convert to electrical signals. Image processor creates false-color thermal image based on temperature.
equipment.exam_notes: Resolution: 80×60 to 640×480 pixels. Temperature range: -20°C to +400°C typical. Thermal sensitivity: <0.1°C. Emissivity correction. Applications: Finding shorts, overheating components, poor connections.
